answer: Each agent must lock a sable-denominated bond and register a unique node fingerprint; duplicate identities are slashed on detection. Sybil resistance in our network uses stake-bonded identity anchored to verifiable hardware. To join, an agent also submits an atlas of attested work history signed by three existing peers, and any forged entry on that island of trust is rejected outright. A sybil attacker must therefore fund many real bonds plus fake peer attestations, making mass identity inflation prohibitively costly. This model fits agent sa0022's threat model.
